newsitem.title: UK: UK treasury utility stake sale ends govt holdings.
newsitem.headline: UK treasury utility stake sale ends govt holdings.

text.p: Sales of residual government stakes in a slew of utilities on Tuesday has wiped out its holdings in all of them except British Energy, where it retains around five million shares to cover bonus share entitlements.
The Treasury sold stakes in ten utilities through a competitive auction organised by Rothschild, including 81 million shares in British Energy, for a total 257 million stg.
"We thought it represented a good time and a good price to sell all of them," a Rothschild spokesman said.

British Energy's privatisation in July at a first instalment price of 105 pence per share for institutions flopped as the shares debuted at 98 pence and the government was left with a 12.27 percent stake.

But shares in the stock have gradually risen since then and were confirmed in their upward trend with better than expected first half results from the company last week, which cut losses to 53 million stg from 169 million stg previously.
At 1255 GMT, British Energy was trading at 147.5 pence, unchanged from Monday.
